title: Chinese Evergreen ( Aglaonema ) Care, Cultivation & Growing Guide

paragraphs.heading: Soil Type: Commercial soilless mix with extra humus
paragraphs.text: Watering: Keep soil moist; allow top 1–2 inches to dry before watering again

paragraphs.heading: Chinese Evergreen Plant Overview
paragraphs.text: Chinese evergreen ( Aglaonema species) is a tropical foliage plant that is one of the most durable houseplants. It tolerates poor light, dry air, air-conditioning, and drought. Chinese evergreens originate from the tropical and subtropical regions of Southeast Asia and New Guinea.

paragraphs.heading: Best Light Conditions
paragraphs.text: Chinese evergreens are remarkably tolerant plants. The solid green cultivars will grow in low light. Variegated types (displaying different colors) with leaves of various colors will need low to moderate light. Low light is mainly found in indirect or heavily shaded indoor areas, while moderate light is bright and indirect. They do not like direct sunlight on their foliage.

paragraphs.heading: Temperature & Humidity
paragraphs.text: Prefer 68 to 80 °F temperature range but tolerates as low as 55 °F

paragraphs.heading: Temperature & Humidity
paragraphs.text: Most grow well in an average house with low to moderate humidity.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Chinese Evergreen
paragraphs.text: Keep the soil constantly moist but not too wet.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Chinese Evergreen
paragraphs.text: It is essential to water the top 1-2 inches of dry soil.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Chinese Evergreen
paragraphs.text: Too much or too little water can damage the roots and hinder growth.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Chinese Evergreen
paragraphs.text: Avoid using water that is too hot or too cold to water Chinese evergreens.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Chinese Evergreen
paragraphs.text: Room temperature water is recommended for watering.

paragraphs.heading: Watering Chinese Evergreen
paragraphs.text: Test by sticking two fingers in the top 2 inches of soil: Dry: Time to water

paragraphs.heading: Cold & damp: Do not water
paragraphs.text: For more information on proper watering practices, see HGIC 1459, Indoor Plants-Watering .

paragraphs.heading: Diseases
paragraphs.text: Root rot usually results from a soil mix that does not drain quickly or from overwatering.

paragraphs.heading: Diseases
paragraphs.text: Powdery mildew can be an issue when there is high humidity.

paragraphs.heading: Other Problems
paragraphs.text: Excessive fertilizer can cause leaf edge burn.

paragraphs.heading: Other Problems
paragraphs.text: Chinese evergreens are sensitive to chilling temperatures below 50 °F.

paragraphs.heading: Chinese Evergreen Toxicity
paragraphs.text: Leaves can be toxic to pets, particularly dogs and cats.

paragraphs.heading: Chinese Evergreen Toxicity
paragraphs.text: Keep household pets away from Aglaonema species.

paragraphs.heading: Chinese Evergreen Toxicity
paragraphs.text: For more information on toxic plants for pets, refer to the ASPCA’s Toxic and Non-Toxic Plants List .

paragraphs.heading: Ribbon Aglaonema ( A. commutatum )
paragraphs.text: ‘Frasher’ has milky green leaves with white petioles (leaf stalks) and cream color mottling on the leaves.

paragraphs.heading: Ribbon Aglaonema ( A. commutatum )
paragraphs.text: ‘Pseudobracteatum’ has leaves spotted with gray and green, and the leaf veins have white highlights.

paragraphs.heading: Ribbon Aglaonema ( A. commutatum )
paragraphs.text: ‘Treubii’ has narrow grayish-green leaves with pale green or yellow-green spots.

paragraphs.heading: Pewter Plant ( A. crispum )
paragraphs.text: Pewter plant is a very robust plant that grows 3 to 4 feet tall with silvery markings on green leaves. It tolerates very low light.

paragraphs.heading: Chinese Evergreen ( A. modestum )
paragraphs.text: Chinese evergreen has shiny, dark green, waxy, and lance-shaped leaves with wavy margins on short stems. It tolerates very low light and low humidity.

paragraphs.heading: Chinese Evergreen ( A. modestum )
paragraphs.text: ‘BJ Freeman’ has grayish and green flecks along the leaf midribs and margins. The light green leaves have grayish-green flecks.

paragraphs.heading: Burmese Evergreen ( A. nitidum )
paragraphs.text: Burmese evergreen has dark green, linear-oblong leaves with leathery leaf blades. The dark green leaves have white splashes, and they can grow up to 3 feet. Burmese evergreen has colorful leaves with deeply channeled petioles, narrowly oblong to oblanceolate-elliptic (leaf gets wider towards the tip and narrows down towards the base).

paragraphs.heading: Camouflage Plant ( A. pictum )
paragraphs.text: Camouflage plant has dark green and variegated leaves that grow up to 2 feet tall and 18 inches wide. It prefers partial or dappled sunlight.

paragraphs.heading: Camouflage Plant ( A. pictum )
paragraphs.text: ‘Tricolor’ has a camouflage pattern of green, silver, and light green foliage.

paragraphs.heading: Hybrid Aglaonema Cultivars
paragraphs.text: A cultivar is a plant selected for a desirable plant trait and is usually man-made. Hybrid cultivars differ slightly, as they result from crossing two different plant species or varieties (different genetic makeup, varieties, etc.) The parent of the hybrid cultivars listed below includes A. crispum, A. commutatum, A. modestum, and A. nitidum . Some of the hybrid cultivars listed below, such as ‘x’, do not have records of their parents.

paragraphs.heading: Hybrid Aglaonema Cultivars
paragraphs.text: ‘Butterfly’ has bright green leaves with yellow specks, pink stripes in the center and pink stems.

paragraphs.heading: Hybrid Aglaonema Cultivars
paragraphs.text: ‘Spring Snow’ has cream colored leaves speckled with a green pattern.

paragraphs.heading: Hybrid Aglaonema Cultivars
paragraphs.text: ‘Suzy’ has low light tolerance, characterized by green leaves and splashes of pink coloring.
